content.text: What is the maximum execution timeout for an AWS Lambda function?
The maximum execution timeout for a Lambda function is 15 minutes.

output.text: The maximum execution timeout for an AWS Lambda function is 15 minutes. The retrieved passage confirms that Lambda supports functions running up to this duration, after which the function execution will be terminated.

content.text: AWS Lambda Overview  AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that runs your code in response to events and automatically manages the underlying compute resources. Lambda functions can be triggered by various AWS services including API Gateway, S3, DynamoDB Streams, SNS, SQS, and EventBridge. Lambda supports multiple programming languages including Python, Node.js, Java, Go, .NET, and Ruby. Each Lambda function runs in its own isolated execution environment. Lambda automatically scales by running code in response to each trigger, processing each trigger individually. You pay only for the compute time you consume, with no charge when your code is not running. The maximum execution timeout for a Lambda function is 15 minutes. Lambda functions can have up to 10 GB of memory allocated. Lambda supports container images up to 10 GB in size as deployment packages.

Amazon S3 Overview  Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) is an object storage service offering industry-leading scalability, data availability, security, and performance. S3 stores data as objects within buckets. An object consists of a file and optionally any metadata that describes that file. S3 offers multiple storage classes designed for different use cases: S3 Standard for frequently accessed data, S3 Intelligent-Tiering for data with unknown or changing access patterns, S3 Standard-IA and S3 One Zone-IA for infrequently accessed data, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long-term archive. S3 provides 99.999999999% (11 nines) of data durability. S3 supports versioning to preserve, retrieve, and restore every version of every object stored in a bucket. S3 bucket names must be globally unique across all AWS accounts.

Amazon DynamoDB Overview  Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database service that provides fast and predictable performance with seamless scalability. DynamoDB supports both key-value and document data models. Tables in DynamoDB are schemaless, meaning each item can have a different set of attributes. DynamoDB uses primary keys to uniquely identify each item in a table. A primary key can be a simple partition key or a composite key consisting of a partition key and a sort key. DynamoDB supports two read consistency models: eventually consistent reads and strongly consistent reads. DynamoDB offers two capacity modes: on-demand and provisioned. DynamoDB Streams captures a time-ordered sequence of item-level modifications in a DynamoDB table. Global tables provide a fully managed solution for deploying a multi-Region, multi-active database. DynamoDB supports transactions with ACID properties across multiple items and tables.
